title: The Old Traveler at the Edge of the Trees

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DEPARTURES AND EXILE (DEP-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Leaving and being left: moving huts, short journeys, visitors going home, goodbyes done well and badly, homesickness, and the rare person who sails away for good. Choosing to leave is never a rejection of one's people, and choosing to stay is never a failure.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult or elder)

collection.description: An old traveler has sat at the edge of the trees for two days, looking at the village: invite them to the fire, or leave food.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: For two days an old traveler has been sitting at the edge of the trees, looking at the village. Not coming in. Not leaving. Just looking. This evening (name1) walks over. The traveler says, quietly, that they were born here, a very long time ago, and left, and wanted to see it once more. They don't say why they left. (name1) doesn't ask.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (name1) offers a place by the fire. The traveler hesitates, then comes. They eat slowly and say very little. A few of the elders peer at them, as if trying to place a face, and nobody quite manages it. In the morning the traveler is gone. There is a small carved fish on the stone where they sat.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (name1) brings a bowl of stew and a blanket and leaves them on a rock nearby. "In case," (he/she) says, and goes back. In the morning the bowl is empty and washed, and the blanket is folded on top of it. The traveler has gone. (name1) never learns who they were, and decides that was their business to keep.
